questions.question: How does ozone behave as a greenhouse gas?
questions.solution_html:
• Ozone present in the atmosphere absorbs infrared radiation emitted from the Earth’s surface. By
  • absorbing this radiation it traps heat within the atmosphere and contributes to the greenhouse effect.
  • This trapped heat increases the temperature of the lower atmosphere and influences climate
  • regulation. Although ozone is essential for absorbing harmful ultraviolet radiation in the stratosphere
  • increased ozone in the lower atmosphere can contribute to atmospheric warming. (Any four valid
  • points, give full credit)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: What is sequestration of CO ?
questions.solution_html:
• Carbon dioxide sequestration refers to the capture and long‑term storage of carbon dioxide from the
  • atmosphere or from industrial emission sources in order to reduce greenhouse gas concentration. The
  • captured CO₂ is prevented from entering the atmosphere and is stored in geological formations, deep
  • saline aquifers, depleted oil and gas reservoirs, or through mineral carbonation processes. This
  • technology is an important strategy for mitigating climate change because it reduces the accumulation
  • of carbon dioxide responsible for global warming. (Definition – (2 marks), methods of storage or role
  • in climate mitigation –(2 marks)).
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: What is ozone depletion? Mention any two causes of ozone layer depletion.
questions.solution_html:
• Ozone depletion refers to the thinning or reduction in the concentration of the ozone layer in the
  • stratosphere. This occurs mainly due to the release of chemical substances that destroy ozone
  • molecules through catalytic reactions. Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) used in refrigerants and aerosols
  • release chlorine radicals in the atmosphere which break down ozone molecules. Other pollutants such
  • as nitrogen oxides, halons and certain industrial chemicals also contribute to the destruction of the
  • ozone layer. (Definition – (2 marks), two causes – (2 marks))
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: What is acid rain? Mention any two causes of acid rain?
questions.solution_html:
• Acid rain refers to precipitation such as rain, snow or fog that contains acidic components with a pH
  • lower than about 5.6. It is mainly produced when sulfur dioxide (SO₂) and nitrogen oxides (NOₓ)
  • released from industrial processes and vehicle emissions react with water vapour in the atmosphere
  • to form sulfuric acid and nitric acid. These acids dissolve in rainwater and fall to the Earth’s surface
  • causing harmful effects on soil, vegetation, aquatic systems and monuments. (Definition – (2 marks)
  • two causes – (2 marks)).
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: List four benefits of biomass utilization in decarbonization.
questions.solution_html:
• List four benefits of biomass utilization in decarbonization.
  • Biomass utilization involves the use of organic materials such as agricultural residues, wood waste
  • and plant materials as energy sources. Biomass is considered renewable because plants absorb carbon
  • dioxide during growth, which offsets the CO₂ released during energy production. The use of biomass
  • reduces dependence on fossil fuels and helps decrease net greenhouse gas emissions. It also supports
  • waste management by converting organic waste into useful energy resources. (Any four valid points
  • give full credit).
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: List four advantages of solar energy.
questions.solution_html:
• List four advantages of solar energy.
  • Solar energy is one of the most abundant and renewable sources of energy available on Earth. It
  • produces electricity without emitting greenhouse gases or air pollutants during operation, making it
  • environmentally friendly. Solar energy systems reduce dependence on fossil fuels and contribute to
  • sustainable energy development. Once installed, solar power systems have relatively low operating
  • and maintenance costs, making them economically beneficial in the long term. (Any four advantages
  • give full credit).
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Define mining.Discuss the purpose of mining.
questions.solution_html:
• Mining is the process of extracting valuable minerals and geological materials from the Earth’s crust.
  • These minerals include metals such as iron, copper and aluminium as well as fuels and industrial
  • materials. Mining provides essential raw materials required for industries, manufacturing
  • construction and technological development. It also plays an important role in economic growth by
  • supporting industrial production and infrastructure development. (Definition – (1 mark), purpose and
  • economic importance – (3 marks)).
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the characteristics of thermosphere and exosphere. / Explain in detail the process of removing CO₂ from the atmosphere using Direct
questions.solution_html:
• The thermosphere is the layer of the atmosphere located above the mesosphere and extends roughly
  • from about 80 km to nearly 700 km above the Earth’s surface. In this region the temperature increases
  • significantly due to the absorption of high‑energy solar radiation. The thermosphere contains the
  • ionosphere, which is rich in charged particles and plays an important role in radio communication
  • and satellite transmission. The density of air molecules is extremely low in this layer. Above the
  • thermosphere lies the exosphere, which is the outermost layer of the atmosphere. In the exosphere
  • atmospheric gases gradually escape into outer space and the density of particles becomes extremely
  • sparse. Hydrogen and helium are the dominant gases present and many artificial satellites orbit within
  • this region. (Thermosphere definition – (1 mark), characteristics – (2.5 marks), exosphere definition – 1
  • characteristics – (2.5 marks),).
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: / Air Capture technology.
questions.solution_html:
• technology.
  • Direct Air Capture (DAC) is an advanced technology designed to remove carbon dioxide directly
  • from the ambient atmosphere. In this process, large volumes of air are passed through specialized
  • chemical filters or sorbent materials that selectively bind with carbon dioxide molecules. Once the
  • CO₂ is captured, the sorbent is heated or chemically treated to release concentrated carbon dioxide
  • gas. The captured CO₂ is then compressed and transported for long‑term storage in geological
  • formations or used in industrial applications such as synthetic fuel production. DAC technology is
  • considered an important tool for reducing atmospheric greenhouse gas concentrations and combating
  • climate change. (Any four valid points, give full credit).
questions.final_answer: climate change. (Any four valid points, give full credit)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss in detail the major causes of water pollution. Classify the different categories of water pollution and explain each with suitable examples.
questions.solution_html:
• pollution and explain each with suitable examples.
  • Water pollution refers to the contamination of water bodies such as rivers, lakes and groundwater by
  • harmful substances that degrade water quality and make it unsafe for human use and aquatic life.
  • Major causes include the discharge of untreated industrial effluents containing heavy metals and toxic
  • chemicals, domestic sewage that introduces pathogens and organic waste and agricultural runoff
  • carrying fertilizers and pesticides. Water pollution can be categorized into biological pollution caused
  • by microorganisms, chemical pollution caused by toxic compounds and thermal pollution caused by
  • the discharge of heated water from industrial plants. These pollutants disrupt aquatic ecosystems and
  • affect human health. (Causes (2 marks), classification (3 marks) explanation with examples (2 marks)).
questions.final_answer: affect human health. (Causes , classification explanation with examples )
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain biomass energy and discuss various biofuels obtained from biomass.
questions.solution_html:
• Biomass energy refers to energy obtained from organic materials such as plant residues, agricultural
  • waste, wood and animal waste. These materials can be converted into useful fuels through processes
  • such as combustion, fermentation and anaerobic digestion. Common biofuels derived from biomass
  • include bioethanol produced by fermentation of sugars from crops such as sugarcane or corn
  • biodiesel produced from vegetable oils or animal fats and biogas produced from the anaerobic
  • digestion of organic waste. Biomass energy is considered renewable and helps reduce reliance on
  • fossil fuels while contributing to sustainable energy production. (Definition – 1, any three biofuel
  • with explanation (6 marks)).
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss metallic and non-metallic mineral resources in detail, with examples and properties.
questions.solution_html:
• Mineral resources are naturally occurring inorganic substances found in the Earth’s crust that are
  • economically valuable. Metallic minerals contain metal elements and are good conductors of heat
  • and electricity; examples include iron, copper and aluminium ores. These minerals are widely used
  • in construction, manufacturing and electrical industries due to properties such as malleability and
  • ductility. Non‑metallic minerals do not contain metals and generally lack metallic properties.
  • Examples include limestone, gypsum, mica and phosphates, which are used in cement production
  • fertilizers, ceramics and other industrial applications. (Definition – 1, metallic minerals examples –
  • (3marks), non‑metallic minerals examples –(3 marks)).
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
